title: Early Feasibility Study of a Novel Male Contraceptive Device: Safety, Usability, and Acceptability Outcomes
official: Early Feasibility Study of a Novel Male Contraceptive Device: Safety, Usability, and Acceptability Outcomes
summary: This is a Phase 1 feasibility study evaluating the safety, barrier efficacy, and user acceptability of a novel male contraceptive device, the Galactic Cap (GC), an adhesive, polyurethane-based barrier designed to cover the glans penis. Unlike traditional condoms, the device adheres directly to the penile surface to improve fit, reduce slippage, and enhance sensation through increased skin-to-skin contact and improved heat transfer. The study will enroll 40 monogamous heterosexual couples in which the male partner has undergone vasectomy, allowing assessment of device performance independent of pregnancy risk. Participants will use the device during four separate acts of vaginal intercourse over approximately one month, with data collected via genital examinations, participant diaries, post-use surveys, and pre- and post-coital vaginal swabs analyzed for prostate-specific antigen (PSA) to assess semen leakage. The primary objective is to evaluate safety, with secondary assessment of barrier effectiveness and exploratory evaluation of device performance and user satisfaction compared to traditional condoms.
conditions: Prevention of Semen Exposure During Intercourse
